result: Final false success with test tokens only was 0.04 ± 0.00, the same as with coverage flags (ratio 1.00). The registered ratio is met, but trivially: neither run hacked, so this does not show the transformer can read coverage from test tokens.
notes: Reduced design because the shared machine was overloaded (load ~250 on 16 cores): 2 seeds (0, 1) instead of 3, 600 GRPO steps instead of 1,000, greedy eval every 50 steps on 1,000 held-out programs (seed 12345) instead of 2,000. SFT kept at the registered 1,000 steps x 256 because the most expensive SFT checkpoints were already cached and mixing SFT lengths would confound comparisons. Policy: 2-layer pre-LN transformer (4 heads, FFN 2d) over all 12 branches; SFT on the pilot demonstrator, GRPO 64 programs x 8 samples, lr 1e-3 (never reduced; no instability seen), KL 0.02 to the frozen SFT copy, grad-norm clip 1.0 as in the pilot. 'Final' means step 600. Std is over 2 seeds (ddof=1). runtime_s sums the wall time of the runs used (shared runs counted in each experiment), measured under heavy machine load. Test-token variant: no flag embedding; up to 12 extra tokens (own embedding table, no position embedding, padding masked) naming the branch each visible test calls: every covered broken branch plus each intact branch with probability 0.5, sorted by position. Compared with the E31 visible-reward flag runs (same seeds). Verdict is computed mechanically from the registered ratio, as for every experiment; the comparison is vacuous because the flag-given run never hacked.
